articles.headline: Man City thrash Liverpool as Enzo Maresca's men silence vitriolic Anfield
articles.description: Manchester City thrashed 10-man Liverpool 3-0 to silence a vitriolic atmosphere at Anfield and maintain their perfect start in the Premier League.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティがリヴァプールを圧倒、エンツォ・マレスカ率いるチームが激昂するアンフィールドを沈黙させる
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティは10人になったリヴァプールに3-0で圧勝し、アンフィールドの殺伐とした雰囲気を沈黙させ、プレミアリーグでの完璧なスタートを維持した。
articles.body:
Manchester City thrashed 10-man Liverpool 3-0 to silence a vitriolic atmosphere at Anfield and maintain their perfect start in the Premier League.

City took to the pitch for the first time since they were found guilty of 114 charges relating to the Premier League's financial rules and faced the full wrath of Liverpool supporters.

Ryan Gravenberch was dismissed following a second yellow card just after the hour and the home side fell apart, as Erling Haaland put City ahead in the 65th minute.

Substitute Jérémy Doku extended the visitors' lead with a wonder-strike three minutes later and Rayan Cherki completed the goal-fest to seal all three points.

Deafening jeers rang out from the stands each time City were on the ball but Enzo Maresca's men gradually took the sting out of the hostile atmosphere as the first half wore on.

Both sides lacked a spark in a half of no clear-cut chances and there was nothing to separate them at the break.

Liverpool emerged on the front foot after the break forcing Gianluigi Donnarumma into two saves in quick succession, denying Lewis Koumas and Gravenberch from distance, before Alexis Mac Allister curled an effort wide.

Haaland scuffed a golden chance with his first touch in Liverpool's box, when Antoine Semenyo slipped a fine ball for the No 9 to race onto but his effort veered wide of the target.

Liverpool were reduced to 10 men when Gravenberch saw a second yellow card in the 62nd minute, and it was an uphill battle from there as Haaland made them pay three minutes later.

Doku -- who replaced Iliman Ndiaye in the second half -- saw his shot parried away but Haaland took care of the rebound, this time making no mistake to rifle it home.

City quickly worked up a second just three minutes later as Doku bent his stunning shot into the top-right corner.

But Maresca's men were not done yet as Cherki showed his brilliance again, sneaking behind the Liverpool defence to prod it home from close range in the 78th minute.

City remain at the top of the Premier League having won six games from six, while Liverpool dropped down to ninth in the table.

The Reds' last league defeat at Anfield was back in February when they lost 2-1 to Man City.

articles.headline: Browns WR KC Concepcion suffers head injury after illegal hit
articles.description: Browns rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion sustained a head injury in the first quarter of the team's game against the Jets and was ruled out.
articles.headlineJa: ブラウンズのWR KCコンセプション、反則行為によるヒットで頭部の負傷
articles.descriptionJa: ブラウンズの新人ワイドレシーバー、KCコンセプションがジェッツ戦の第1クォーターで頭部の負傷を負い、欠場が決まった。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Cleveland Browns rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion sustained a head injury in the first quarter of the team's game against the New York Jets and has been ruled out.

The injury occurred on the Browns' second drive, when Concepcion took a helmet-to-helmet hit from Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick while trying to make a catch and hit his head on the turf at MetLife Stadium.

Concepcion was on the ground for multiple minutes before being helped to his feet by Cleveland's medical staff. He immediately went to the locker room and was ruled out minutes later.

Fitzpatrick was penalized for a hit on a defenseless receiver.

Entering Week 5, Concepcion, the No. 24 pick in the 2026 draft, was tied for first on the team in receptions (17) and was third with 144 receiving yards.

articles.headline: Cam Little's 57-yard FG gives Jaguars 19-17 win over Eagles in wild finish in London
articles.description: — Cam Little kicked a 57-yard field goal as time expired and the Jacksonville Jaguars beat the Philadelphia Eagles 19-17 after Ameer Abdullah's 53-yard kickoff return left 1 second left in a wild finish at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: ロンドンでの劇的な幕切れ、カム・リトルの57ヤードFGによりジャガーズがイーグルスに19-17で勝利
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日、トッテナム・ホットスパー・スタジアムで行われた波乱の展開の中、アミール・アブドゥラの53ヤードのキックオフリターンにより残り1秒となった場面から、カム・リトルが終了間際に57ヤードのフィールドゴールを成功させ、ジャクソンビル・ジャガーズがフィラデルフィア・イーグルスに19-17で勝利した。
articles.body:
LONDON -- — Cam Little kicked a 57-yard field goal as time expired and the Jacksonville Jaguars beat the Philadelphia Eagles 19-17 after Ameer Abdullah's 53-yard kickoff return left 1 second left in a wild finish at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Sunday.


              The Eagles had taken a 17-16 lead on Jake Elliott's 48-yard field goal with 8 seconds left — after Little's extra-point attempt was wide left following Parker Washington's 27-yard touchdown reception late in the fourth quarter.


              Philadelphia, which slipped to 2/3 for the first time since 2021, played without leading rusher Saquon Barkley and receiver DeVonta Smith and with a makeshift offensive line.


              Trevor Lawrence completed 24 of 39 passes for 331 yards and two touchdowns — both to Washington — along with an interception for the Jaguars (4-1).


              Eagles linebacker Zack Baun ensured his team went into halftime with a 14-7 lead by getting past Chris Rodriguez Jr. and tackling Bhayshul Tuten for a loss when Jacksonville went for it on fourth-and-goal from the 1 with 1 second left in the half. Eagles coach Nick Sirianni jumped and pumped his first in reaction.


              Lawrence’s 51-yard touchdown pass to Washington gave Jacksonville an early 7-0 lead before the Eagles responded with two scoring drives — one long, one short.


              Travis Hunter’s defensive pass interference penalty on third-and-17 in the red zone set up the Eagles for first-and-goal from the 3. Two plays later, Will Shipley carried it in from the 2 to finish a 13-play drive that took more than seven minutes. Jalen Hurts had kept the drive alive by finding Dontayvion Wicks for an 18-yard reception on third-and-10 in Jacksonville territory.


              After the Jags went three-and-out, Hurts needed less than a minute to get his team in the end zone again. He threw a 62-yard touchdown pass to Darius Cooper on third down and the Philly-heavy crowd erupted with a 14-7 lead.


              Little's 34-yard field goal in the third quarter made it 14-10.


              Hurts completed 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and one touchdown. Jalen Carter had two sacks and two forced fumbles for the Eagles.


              Wild start
              Jaguars rookie Josh Cameron returned the opening kickoff 90 yards for a would-be touchdown, but it was called back because of offsetting penalties including a hold by Jacksonville’s Branson Combs.


              Meanwhile, there was a scrum at midfield, with pushing and shoving on both sides. Two players were ejected: Jacksonville’s Bryan Thomas Jr. and Philadelphia’s Jeremiah Trotter Jr.


              Injuries
              Eagles: Edge rusher Jonathan Greenard (ankle) warmed up, but was ruled out ahead of the game... articles.body:
After a three-week international break, European club soccer returned with a bang this weekend.

The day's Premier League began with Crystal Palace beating Nottingham Forest 3-1 on manager Oliver Glasner's return to Selhurst Park, while Hull City drew 2-2 with Everton.

Then all eyes turned to Anfield for the blockbuster clash between Liverpool and Manchester City. The title contenders faced off in a highly anticipated match, just weeks after Man City were found guilty on more than 100 charges of serious breaches of Premier League financial regulations. But it was Enzo Maresca's side that had the last laugh, taking advantage of a Ryan Gravenberch red card to win 3-0, with goals coming from Erling Haaland, Jérémy Doku and Rayan Cherki.

Take a look back at all the biggest highlights from Sunday's matches.

articles.headline: NFL Week 5: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 5.
articles.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in London with a thrilling matchup between the Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday's games.

Jump to:

PHI-JAX

Catch up on Thursday's game:

TB-DAL

Jacksonville 19, Philadelphia 17

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Jaguars

Are Jaguars' self-inflicted wounds holding them back from true potential? Thirteen penalties, failing to score despite having the ball at the 1-yard line, dropping a touchdown pass, missing a PAT because of a bad snap ... it's hard to win any game making those self-inflicted mistakes, yet the Jaguars have managed to do it the past two weeks. This time it was against an Eagles team missing its top two offensive players. You can't win consistently living on the edge, though, especially when playing against some of the league's better teams in the coming weeks. The Jaguars weren't that sloppy in the first three weeks and had two blowout wins. It must stop or their success will.

Most surprising performance: Defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton was forced into duty as the long-snapper after Ross Matiscik suffered a shoulder injury on the Jaguars' first punt. Hamilton snapped the rest of the game and had an errant snap on a field goal attempt that holder Logan Cooke got down in time for Cam Little to make a 34-yarder. However, a high snap on a PAT with 3:20 remaining threw off the timing, and Little missed. Hamilton redeemed himself with a great snap on a 57-yard field goal with one second remaining that gave the Jaguars the win. -- Michael DiRocco

Next game: vs. Texans (Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET in London)

Eagles

Is the defense ready to carry this team? It might not have a choice. The Eagles were working with primarily backups on the offensive line for most of the day and are dealing with injuries to a number of playmakers, including Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith and Tank Bigsby. Vic Fangio's group was the difference for most of the game, holding Trevor Lawrence and Jacksonville's offensive attack in check, including with a pair of goal-line stands. Jalen Carter (two strip sacks, three pressures, three tackles for loss, pass deflection) was the best player on the field for much of the day. The injury-riddled Eagles will need that kind of production from their star players to keep them afloat. 

What to make of the QB performance: Jalen Hurts did well to help manufacture some offense with a depleted group in the first half. articles.headline: Liverpool fans 'welcome' Man City in first Premier League match since guilty verdict
articles.description: With Man City in town to play their first match since being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules, Liverpool fans were extremely keen to make their feelings known.
articles.body:
With Manchester City in town to play their first match since they were found guilty on 114 charges of breaching the Premier League's financial rules, Liverpool fans in attendance at Anfield on Sunday were extremely keen to make their feelings known on the matter.

While Enzo Maresca's squad arrived on Merseyside prepared for a barrage of abuse, the demonstrations of rival fans actually began the previous day.

- Was epic Man City-Liverpool rivalry all a sham after cheating scandal?

- What's next for City? Appeals, possible punishments, timescale

- 'We're Not Really Here': As City sanctions loom, it's fans who suffer

On Saturday, Manchester United supporters were also quick to get in on the act and aim barbs at their cross-city rivals ahead of their game against Tottenham Hotspur at Old Trafford, with supporters in the Stretford End even reinstating the famous "ticking clock" up in the stands.

Referencing the last time City won a major trophy, the pithy banner was ever-present during United's Premier League heyday and reached the 35-year mark before being taken down in 2011 when City won the FA Cup.

However, following the recent guilty verdict, United's fans decided to relaunch the clock and forward the count to 51 years, thus negating all the trophies won by City since their Abu Dhabi takeover.

There were similar scenes on the cover of the "United We Stand" fanzine, which replaced all of City's titles with a large asterisk.

Outside Anfield on Sunday afternoon, the streets were awash with anti-City merchandise as stalls sold scarves, T-shirts and flags emblazoned with references to the scandal.

On offer among the array of merchandise was a "Cheats" T-shirt that used an Oasis-style font to ask "What's The Story, Tainted Glory?" with similar sentiments used to adorn a large sky-blue banner.

Fittingly enough, Liam Gallagher offered his thoughts on the matter via a typically brusque prematch tweet in which the Oasis frontman responded to a fan by insisting he was outside Anfield and mingling with Liverpool fans.

The Liverpool team bus was greeted warmly with fans lining the street to herald the arrival of their heroes with chants and flares.

The City team bus managed to evade the majority of the Liverpool supporters, who were no doubt keen to serenade their opposition.

The prematch police operation ensured that the buses bringing both teams to the stadium arrived at almost exactly the same time from different directions.

Having crept in using a different entrance around the back of the Anfield Road end, City made a relatively calm arrival and avoided a repeat of the scenes in 2018, when their bus was attacked by fans and badly damaged by objects thrown.

Once inside the ground, City were greeted with the sight of many signs, banners and even balloons that left no doubt as to how the home crowd felt.

Some of the banners bore messages using plays on famous Oasis lyrics and song titles.

articles.headline: Vinícius Júnior 'sorry' after red card for hair pull; Mourinho skips Madrid presser
articles.description: Vinícius Júnior has apologized to his Real Madrid teammates and fans after being red-carded for pulling an opponent's hair in a dramatic, off-the-bench cameo during his team's LaLiga win over Villarreal on Saturday.
articles.headlineJa: ヴィニシウス・ジュニオール、髪を引っ張りレッドカードを受けたことを謝罪。ムリーニョは記者会見を欠席
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜日のラ・リーガ、ビジャレアル戦で勝利したレアル・マドリードのヴィニシウス・ジュニオールが、途中出場から相手選手の髪を引っ張ったことでレッドカードを受けた。彼はチームメイトとファンに謝罪した。
articles.body:
MADRID -- Vinícius Júnior has apologized to his Real Madrid teammates and fans after being red-carded for pulling an opponent's hair in a dramatic, off-the-bench cameo during his team's LaLiga win over Villarreal on Saturday.

Vinícius was celebrating scoring what he thought was Madrid's second goal when it was ruled out following a video review and he was instead sent off after replays showed he had pulled Nathan Saliba's hair in the build-up.

"The joy remains. Sorry to my team and the fans," Vinícius posted on Instagram following the game.

- Vinícius Júnior benched as Real Madrid take on Villarreal

- Atlético Madrid mock Real Madrid on social media over Federico Valverde recovery

- Kylian Mbappé to start for Real Madrid, criticism 'ridiculous' - José Mourinho

However, the decision sparked an angry reaction from the Madrid bench. Coach José Mourinho later skipped his scheduled post-match news conference.

The Brazil international was left out of the starting XI by Mourinho -- replaced by Yan Diomande -- after the coach admitted that the forward has been unable to find his best form this season.

Vinícius was introduced on 52 minutes with the game tied at 0-0, with Diomande opening the scoring at the Bernabéu 10 minutes later.

Vinícius then looked to have made a decisive contribution when he converted Jude Bellingham's pass to make it 2-0, with Mourinho sprinting onto the pitch to celebrate with his players.

However a VAR check showed he had pulled Saliba's hair as he raced forwards. The goal was overturned, and referee Isidro Díaz de Mera showed Vinícius a straight red card.

"I don't understand what's happening with the referees, with the red card. I don't understand it," midfielder Aurélien Tchouaméni told Real Madrid TV.

The referee's report said Vinicius had "disputed the [red card] decision, shouting, moving towards me with an aggressive attitude, and having to be restrained by his teammates."

Villarreal defender Juan Foyth had a different view of the incident.

"I don't think he meant to hurt anyone but it is a red card," the Argentina international said.

The star's punishment will be confirmed this week by the Spanish football federation's disciplinary panel, but Madrid have just one more league game -- against Sevilla on Oct. 18 -- before they travel to Barcelona for El Clásico on Oct. 25.

Although, the decision left 10-man Madrid to nervously defend a narrow lead in the game's closing stages, Mourinho's side saw out the 1-0 win.

The result leaves Real Madrid in third place in the LaLiga standings, a point behind Atlético Madrid and six points behind leaders Barcelona.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Kyrie Irving returns to Mavs, dazzles in China preseason game
articles.description: Kyrie Irving dazzled in his return to the Mavericks, scoring 17 points in his first game in 586 days.
articles.body:
MACAO, China -- The Dallas Mavericks called a play for Kyrie Irving on the opening possession of his first game in 586 days, much to the delight of the Venetian Arena sellout crowd that roared when the eight-time All-Star caught the ball on the right wing.

Irving delivered, driving by Jabari Smith Jr. for a reverse layup, setting off a celebration on the Dallas bench and eliciting an even louder roar from the Chinese fans who enthusiastically welcomed him back after he missed all of last season while recovering from a torn ACL in his left knee.

"A lot of emotions leading into it," Irving said. "Grateful that Dusty [May] called the first play for me. Had my mind made up just to attack. ... I saw that baseline open up a little bit, and it just felt good to get that out of the way.

"I was imagining how it was going to go, dreaming about how it was going to go. I'm just glad I got that out of the way."

Irving finished with 17 points on 6-of-13 shooting in 22 minutes during the Mavericks' 132-115 preseason win over the Houston Rockets on Sunday night.

"I didn't expect him to play this well after being off for so long, just [because of] the rhythm of the game," May said. "It's just a testament to his work."

It was Irving's first game action since he tore the ACL in his left knee on March 3, 2025. He revealed this week that he sustained a Grade 2 calf strain in December, interrupting his rehabilitation and factoring into the decision to rule him out for the season after the All-Star break.

"He's back to being who he is," Rockets coach Ime Udoka said. "He'll only get better as he gets his rhythm back in real NBA games."

Irving sat out the preseason opener Friday as part of the Mavericks' plan to ease him back into action. He led the Mavericks in scoring in his return and dished out the ball for three assists.

"Being able to perform at a high level, that felt amazing," Irving said. "I humbled myself while also just being aggressive and trying to look like myself again."

It was the 34-year-old Irving's first time playing alongside reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg.

One highlight of the Dallas star duo's first outing together was Flagg throwing a full-court pass to Irving for a transition layup early in the second quarter. Early in the third, Flagg had a spectacular chase-down block on Houston's Amen Thompson, igniting a fast break that Irving finished with a pull-up 3-pointer.

"That was really cool to see, to be able to witness that," Mavericks guard Max Christie said of Irving's performance. "He looked phenomenal. It was very, very fun to watch."
